question: A customer support director wants to justify a Claude-based ticket triage pilot to executives and asks how to frame its value. What is the best way to present this business case?
options: A) Present only the model's technical architecture details, since executives mainly evaluate proposals on implementation specifics.
B) Present concrete metrics such as reduced average handling time and ticket deflection rate compared against the current process.
C) Present a claim that the pilot requires no evaluation period, since Claude's output quality never needs to be measured.
D) Present the pilot as guaranteed to eliminate the entire support team's workload within the first month of deployment.
correct_answers: B) Present concrete metrics such as reduced average handling time and ticket deflection rate compared against the current process.
explanations: Incorrect. Executives generally care about business outcomes and ROI more than low-level technical architecture, so this framing misses the audience's priorities.
Correct. Framing value in terms of measurable business outcomes, such as handling time or deflection rate, gives executives a concrete basis for evaluating the pilot against the current process.
Incorrect. Skipping evaluation removes the evidence needed to demonstrate value and identify quality issues before wider rollout.
Incorrect. Promising complete elimination of the team's workload overstates the technology's impact and sets an unrealistic expectation.
